title: Identity normalization of finite-coefficient pro-etale derived pullback
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $A$ a finite commutative ring. Use the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], its constant ring sheaf $A_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and the inverse image and canonical coefficient map $c_A^{\operatorname{id}_X}:(\operatorname{id}_X)^{-1}A_X\to A_X$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Write $e_X:(\operatorname{id}_X)^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}$ for the objectwise identity comparison for sheaves of [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image](1), obtained from $X\times_XU\cong U$. Then $e_{X,A_X}=c_A^{\operatorname{id}_X}$ as ring-sheaf morphisms. For every sheaf $M$ of $A_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the comparison $e_{X,M}$, with the source action transported along $c_A^{\operatorname{id}_X}$, is $A_X$-linear and gives a natural isomorphism $(\operatorname{id}_X)^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}M$. For the derived pullback of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] there is a natural isomorphism
$$
 L(\operatorname{id}_X)^*\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}_{D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A_X)}.
$$
Its component on any cochain representative $M^\bullet$ is represented by the termwise maps $e_{X,M^j}$, after the canonical scalar-transport identification of module pullback. This holds for the zero ring and for the empty scheme as well.

source.place: Tag 09A5 (section-morphism); identity morphism specialization of site inverse image, extracted from returned proof Step 5. Agent-written module and derived normalization; compare lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image(1) and def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations.

proof.text: Put $f=\operatorname{id}_X$, $L=f^{-1}$, $R=f_*$ and $B=A_X$. Specializing [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image](1) gives $e:L\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}$, natural in sheaves and site objects. Its normalization can be read directly in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]: for $U\to X$, the pair $(U,\delta_U:U\to X\times_XU)$ is initial in $\mathcal I_U$, since the unique arrow to $(V,\phi)$ is $a=\operatorname{pr}_2\phi:U\to V$. Indeed its two projections force $u_f(a)\delta_U=\phi$ and determine $a$. Thus it is terminal in $\mathcal I_U^{\mathrm{op}}$. The maps from the colimit to $F(U)$ send the coprojection of $s\in F(V)$ at $(V,\phi)$ to $a^*s$; their inverse is the coprojection at $(U,\delta_U)$. Both composites are identities by the cocone equations. These maps commute with restrictions and sheaf morphisms. Their target is already the sheaf $F$, so the sheafification universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] gives exactly $e_F$. For abelian or ring sheaves all maps here are restriction homomorphisms, so $e_F$ is an isomorphism in the corresponding algebraic category.

source.place: Tag 09A5 (section-morphism), identity specialization; explicit terminal-index formula for the specified inverse image

proof.text: Compute the adjoint $\widetilde e_B:B\to RB$ of $e_B:LB\to B$. By the colimit/sheafification adjunction in [lem-weil-pbc-continuous-functor-sheaf-pullback-adjunction], the unit on $s\in B(V)$ is the coprojection indexed by $(V,\operatorname{id}_{u_f(V)})$, followed by sheafification. This formula follows from the adjunction bijection: a map out of the colimit is evaluated on that coprojection to obtain its adjunct. Step 1 then gives $\widetilde e_{B,V}(s)=\operatorname{pr}_2^*(s)\in B(X\times_XV)$. In particular the image of each constant $a\in A$ is the same constant section on $X\times_XV$. The map $\rho_A^f:B\to RB$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] has exactly those values on the constant presheaf. Since $B$ is its sheafification [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], uniqueness in [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] gives $\widetilde e_B=\rho_A^f$. The ring adjunction of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] has the same unit as the underlying sheaf adjunction, and Step 1 already made $e_B$ a ring map. Taking adjuncts therefore proves $e_B=c_A^f$ as ring-sheaf morphisms, with the specified coefficient map, not just some isomorphism $LB\cong B$.

source.place: Tags 00VE (lemma-adjoints-u), 00WX (lemma-adjoint-sheaves), 00WH (proposition-sheafification-adjoint); unit and constant-presheaf uniqueness calculation

proof.text: Let $M$ be a $B$-module sheaf, with action $\mu:B\times M\to M$ as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The inverse-image action in [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] is $L\mu$ under $L(B\times M)\cong LB\times LM$. Naturality of $e$ with the two projections identifies $e_{B\times M}$ with $e_B\times e_M$: the two projection composites agree, which determines a map to a product. Naturality with $\mu$ therefore gives, on every site object, $e_M(t\cdot m)=e_B(t)\cdot e_M(m)$. Naturality with addition and zero gives the analogous additive identities; alternatively Step 1 already gives an abelian-sheaf isomorphism. By Step 2, transporting the source action to $B$ means $b\cdot m=(c_A^f)^{-1}(b)\cdot m$, whence $e_M(b\cdot m)=b\cdot e_M(m)$. Its inverse is linear too: substitute $m=e_M^{-1}(z)$ in this equality. Thus $e_M:(LM)^{(c_A^f)}\to M$ is an isomorphism of $B$-module sheaves. Naturality for a module morphism follows from naturality for its underlying sheaf map, and the maps commute with all restrictions.

source.place: Tag 03D1 (lemma-pullback-module); naturality with the action and product projections, written explicitly

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-sheaf-scalar-extension-ring-iso] with the small site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], ring sheaves $LB,B$, ring isomorphism $c=c_A^f=e_B$, and $LB$-module $LM$. Its specified isomorphism $\theta:LM\otimes_{LB,c}B\to(LM)^{(c)}$ sends the sheafification image of $m\otimes b$ to $c^{-1}(b)m$ and has inverse $m\mapsto m\otimes1$. By the definition of module pullback [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], the source is $f^*M$. Compose $\theta$ with the linear isomorphism of Step 3 to obtain $\alpha_M:f^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}M$. On these tensor generators it is $m\otimes b\mapsto b\,e_M(m)$, and its inverse is $z\mapsto e_M^{-1}(z)\otimes1$, interpreted through the sheafification unit. Naturality of $\theta$ and of $e$ gives a natural isomorphism $\alpha:f^*\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}_{\operatorname{Mod}(B)}$. In particular, after the specified scalar-transport identification its component is exactly $e_M$.

Write $F=f^*$ on the abelian category $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(B)$ of [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Step 4 identifies $F$ naturally with the identity. Hence $F$ is additive (conjugate $F(h+k)$ by the components of $\alpha$ and use $h+k$), and preserves kernels and cokernels: conjugating any candidate kernel or cokernel diagram by $\alpha$ gives the original diagram with its universal property. Thus it is exact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] to obtain the termwise functor $C(F)$ preserving quasi-isomorphisms and its derived factorization. For a cochain complex $M^\bullet$, naturality of $\alpha$ with each differential gives $d_M^j\alpha_{M^j}=\alpha_{M^{j+1}}F(d_M^j)$. Therefore $(\alpha_{M^j})_j:C(F)M^\bullet\to M^\bullet$ is an isomorphism of complexes, its inverse being the termwise inverse. The same naturality equation with a cochain map shows that these complex isomorphisms form a natural isomorphism $C(F)\cong\operatorname{id}$.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor); termwise exact functor and differential naturality

proof.text: Let $Q:\mathrm{CoCh}(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal A)$ be the localization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. By [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations], in this identified-coefficient situation $Lf^*$ is the exact termwise descent, so it comes with $\varphi_M:Lf^*(QM)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(C(F)M)$. Both $Q\circ C(F)$ and $Q$ invert quasi-isomorphisms, the first by Step 5 and the second by definition of $Q$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property](2) to the natural isomorphism $Q(\alpha^\bullet):Q\circ C(F)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$ of Step 5 and the two factorizations $Lf^*$ and $\operatorname{id}_{D(\mathcal A)}$. It gives a natural isomorphism $Lf^*\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}_{D(\mathcal A)}$ whose component at $QM$ is $Q(\alpha_M^\bullet)\circ\varphi_M$. The inverse descends from the termwise inverse, and the composites are identities by the identity/composition clause of the same localization lemma. Thus on every cochain representative the comparison is represented by the termwise $e_{M^j}$ after the scalar-transport identification of Step 4, as required. This uses the unbounded localization and imposes no boundedness or constructibility condition.

source.place: Tag 04VG (lemma-properties-left-localization) and the cited natural-transformation localization lemma; Mathlib Localization/Predicate.lean:278-364

proof.text: No step assumes that $1\ne0$ in $A$, uses a nonempty site object, or requires a point of $X$. For $A=0$ all unitary $A_X$-module sheaves are zero, and the same action, tensor and comparison formulas apply. For $X=\varnothing$, the sheaf axiom for the empty covering makes the value of every sheaf of sets the singleton and of every abelian sheaf the zero group; the constant ring sheaf is the zero ring sheaf. The displayed maps are then the unique maps, and their inverse and naturality identities remain valid. In particular the argument includes the case where both degeneracies occur.
